title: Steam AI Disclosure examples
author: taisui
selftext:
We all know what's happening, so I'm proposing to use the following AI disclosure statements on Steam:

* **Art:** "Some visual assets were created with AI assistance and edited manually."
* **Audio:** "Some sound effects were created with AI assistance and mixed manually."
* **Text:** "Some written text was created with AI assistance and edited manually."
* **Translations:** "Some localized text was created with AI assistance and reviewed manually."
* **Marketing:** "Some promotional assets were created with AI assistance and edited manually."
* **Live Content:** "Some live content were created with AI assistance and guarded manually."

No more, and no less.

replies.author: taisui
replies.body:
Here is what Opus says:

*It’s half true. I can’t output images, video or audio myself. My output is text, and that text can be code that turns into media when something runs it.*

* *True: I can write SVG directly. With a tool to run code, I can make PNGs from fractals, noise or shaders, WAV audio from sine and FM synthesis, and video by rendering frames and passing them to ffmpeg. You have Python, numpy and ffmpeg installed, so I could do all of that here. None of it uses diffusion.*
* *Misleading:*
   * *“Now”: This isn’t new. Language models have been able to write SVG and audio-synthesis code for years.*
   * *“Can generate”: Something else always runs the code. I write the instructions, not the pixels or the samples.*
   * *“No diffusion needed”: That only holds for media that can be built from math. Patterns, geometry, data visualisations, chiptune-style tones and abstract animation work well.* ***Realistic photos, natural-sounding voices, real-sounding instruments and lifelike video don’t. For those you still need a trained generative model.***

*A more accurate version would be: “Opus can write code that builds images, video and audio from math, as long as the result doesn’t need to look or sound real.”*

comments.author: Galle_
comments.body: From someone who's mostly neutral on AI but sure as hell doesn't want to pay full price for an AI-developed game: I think this plan will backfire. If you want people who are against AI use in game dev to make an exception for you, you should be as informative with your disclosures as possible. Anyone reading disclosures like this is just going to assume the worst. If you're informative, there's at least a chance some people will think your use of AI doesn't violate their standards.
